title: Board of Governors closed for New Year's Day (observed) while the NYSE, the OCC and the Reserve Banks stay open — a full trading session, a quarter-end expiration, and no Fed publishing desk
source: EST: federalreserve.gov/aboutthefed/k8.htm, 'K.8 - Holidays Observed by the Federal Reserve System 2026-2030', re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 82,205 bytes, stamp 'Last Update: July 8, 2026') by this event's own initial research — same byte count as the fomc-minutes-2027-12-29 adjacency sweep that proposed it on 2026-09-08, and re-parsed from scratch rather than inherited. The page states the split rule verbatim in its own header: 'For holidays falling on Saturday, Federal Reserve Banks and Branches will be open the preceding Friday; however, the Board of Governors will be closed.' Its first footnote then names this exact date without inference: 'Saturday - the Federal Reserve Banks are open, but the Board of Governors is closed on July 3, 2026, June 18, 2027, December 24, 2027, December 31, 2027, and November 10, 2028.' The same page carries a dated correction showing the Board revisited this specific observance: 'On July 8, 2026, the first footnote was updated to reflect the observance date for New Year's Day from December 31, 2028, to December 31, 2027.' Its 2028 table column reads New Year's Day 'January 1*', the asterisk being that footnote. THE MARKET SIDE IS THE OPPOSITE AND IS ALSO PRIMARY-SOURCED. nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars, re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200 after its 302, 109,180 bytes), gives no 2028 New Year's row at all and states why verbatim: 'Because the holiday falls on Saturday, January 1, 2028, no New Year's Day holiday is observed.' Its only December early-close footnote across 2026/2027/2028 names 'Thursday, December 24, 2026', so 2027-12-31 is a FULL regular NYSE session, not a half day. optionseducation.org/api/expirationcalendar (HTTP 200, 34,871 bytes, 'accurate as of 1/2/2026') independently agrees on both counts: no holiday flag on 2027-12-31, and the date carries legend type 812CD242-1E6F-48D4-A1CB-9608ABD8344F = 'Quarterly Expiration date' — the last-business-day-of-quarter marker, DISTINCT from the monthly equity/index expiration it puts on 2027-12-17 and the monthly volatility-products expiration on 2027-12-15. Filed estimate on this lane's standing no-self-confirm limit and because this calendar's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no member for an agency's own internal holiday schedule as distinct from a market calendar. THE DATE IS NOT IN DOUBT — three independent primaries agree and the observance is fixed by 5 U.S.C. 6103(b) plus the Board's own published Saturday rule; the estimate label is about the taxonomy. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-09 by this event's initial research (docs/research/events/fed-board-closure-2027-12-31.md) after reading the single prior proposal, proposals/fed-board-closure-2027-12-31.from-fomc-minutes-2027-12-29.json, which is now inert. Every claim above was re-derived from primaries rather than inherited. NOTHING TRADEABLE IS CLAIMED: symbols is empty, no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is calendar- or expiration-keyed, and the research reached a stand-aside on all four horizons. WHY THE ROW EXISTS — and it is a narrower reason than the proposal gave. It is load-bearing for fomc-minutes-2027-12-29, whose whole displacement rule is measured as a gap in days from THIS date (that lane sits at gap -2 and its rule is 0-for-14 at |gap| >= 2), so without this row the mechanism is unauditable from the calendar. THE PROPOSAL'S UNIQUENESS CLAIM IS CORRECTED HERE. It said 'every other Fed-Board closure this calendar would ever carry coincides with a market closure'; that is refuted. The Board is closed with a full NYSE session running on EVERY Columbus Day and EVERY Veterans Day, three of which this calendar already tracks from the bond side (sifma-bond-market-closure-2026-10-12, -2026-11-11, -2027-11-11) — on those days, though, the Reserve Banks are closed too, so the Fed is entirely shut rather than only its publishing desk. The correct rare class is BOARD-ONLY DARK, which requires a federal holiday on a Saturday, and K.8's own footnote makes it exactly two dates in the 2026-2030 window: 2027-12-31 and 2028-11-10 (proposed in the same PR as proposals/fed-board-closure-2028-11-10.from-fed-board-closure-2027-12-31.json). What distinguishes 2027-12-31 is the pile-up on one session: the year's final NYSE session, an OCC quarter-end expiration, Fedwire and the Reserve Banks operating, a bond tape SIFMA recommends shut at 14:00 ET (sifma-bond-early-close-2027-12-31, estimate), and no holiday behind it to absorb any of it, because Saturday New Year is not observed. AND THE MATERIALITY IS A REFUSAL, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED. The Board's own release archive was probed by release date: H.4.1 — the weekly balance sheet, the one Fed number a rates desk watches — has a THURSDAY slot (federalreserve.gov/releases/h41/20260903/ HTTP 200 vs 20260904/ HTTP 404) and published on Thursday December 30 in all three prior instances of this configuration (h41/20041230, 20101230, 20211230 all HTTP 200; the matching Dec-31 URLs all 404). 2027-12-30 is a Thursday, so the closure displaces no Fed print the market prices. The only weekly Board release whose slot IS this Friday is H.8, commercial-bank assets and liabilities, and it moved off every Board-closure Dec 31 the archive reaches (h8/19991231, 20041231, 20101231, 20211231 all 404; seven matched control year-end Fridays with no Board closure all 200). Proposed as an estimate; estimate widens caution and licenses no entry.
